items.hed: The Texans officially ruled out four players for Sunday's Week 12 home game against Baltimore — wide receiver Kayshon Boutte, edge rusher Danielle Hunter, tight end Brevin Jordan and lineman Keylan Rutledge — after Friday's practice report posted game-status designations for the first time this week
items.insight: The Texans' own injury-report page, re-checked same-turn this afternoon, now shows Friday practice data and game statuses: Boutte (hip), Hunter (hamstring), Jordan (finger/foot) and Rutledge (neck/shoulder) are all listed OUT after sitting out practice all week. Defensive tackle Sheldon Rankins (ankle), who did not practice Wednesday, progressed to limited Thursday and full Friday participation and carries no designation beyond unspecified; tight end Dalton Schultz (illness) also progressed to full Friday participation. Linebacker Jacob Hummel (abdomen/groin) is listed Questionable. No other Texans carry a game-status designation ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Ravens at NRG Stadium.
items.image_caption: NRG Stadium (formerly Reliant Stadium), Houston. Venue still.

items.hed: New Astros general manager Randy Flores has begun reshaping a Houston outfield that posted the majors' second-worst OPS last season, outrighting Joey Loperfido and non-tendering Taylor Trammell as his first moves toward an upgrade
items.insight: MLB.com reports the Astros' outfield produced a .662 OPS last season, ranking 29th out of 30 teams, and that Flores has started addressing it by outrighting Loperfido and non-tendering Trammell, clearing roster space as the offseason's bigger outfield additions are still to come. The moves follow new manager Brad Ausmus' coaching-staff hires, which now include J.P. Martinez at pitching coach and Aaron Bates at hitting coach. A same-turn check of the Astros' own news page found nothing newer than a Nov. 26 season-review feature with no new Astros-specific transaction since this morning's board.
items.image_caption: Daikin Park (formerly Minute Maid Park), 2010. Venue still.

items.hed: The Houston Rockets, fresh off a 116-104 win over Phoenix at Toyota Center behind Kevin Durant's season-high 32 points, host the Philadelphia 76ers Friday night at 8:30 p.m. ET in their next game since the holiday break
items.insight: NBA.com's official schedule, re-checked same-turn this afternoon, confirms no Rockets game has been played since the Nov. 25 win over the Suns and lists Friday's 8:30 p.m. ET tip-off against Philadelphia at Toyota Center as the next game on the slate. Center Alperen Sengun recorded his third triple-double of the season in that Suns win per the team's own fantasy-news notes, with forwards Tari Eason (listed as 'Thompson' in the team feed) and Jabari Smith Jr. also logging strong two-way performances; Phoenix shot just 1 of its last 24 three-point attempts down the stretch. Devin Booker led the Suns with 25 points in the loss.
